title: The urban heat island
scene: A professor gives a lecture on why cities are hotter, then takes a question

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 各位同学，今天我们讨论一个与每个城市居民都密切相关的现象：城市热岛效应。
lines.py: Gèwèi tóngxué, jīntiān wǒmen tǎolùn yí ge yǔ měi ge chéngshì jūmín dōu mìqiè xiāngguān de xiànxiàng: chéngshì rèdǎo xiàoyìng.
lines.en: Today we'll discuss something that concerns everyone who lives in a city: the urban heat island effect.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 所谓热岛效应，是指城市中心区域的气温明显高于周边郊区的现象。在一些大城市，夏天夜间的温差甚至可以达到五六度。
lines.py: Suǒwèi rèdǎo xiàoyìng, shì zhǐ chéngshì zhōngxīn qūyù de qìwēn míngxiǎn gāo yú zhōubiān jiāoqū de xiànxiàng. Zài yìxiē dà chéngshì, xiàtiān yèjiān de wēnchā shènzhì kěyǐ dádào wǔ liù dù.
lines.en: The heat island effect means that temperatures in the city centre are clearly higher than in the surrounding suburbs. In some big cities the difference on summer nights can reach five or six degrees.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 造成这一现象的原因是多方面的。首先，城市里大量的道路和建筑使用水泥、玻璃等材料，这些材料白天吸收热量，夜间再缓慢地释放出来。
lines.py: Zàochéng zhè yí xiànxiàng de yuányīn shì duō fāngmiàn de. Shǒuxiān, chéngshì li dàliàng de dàolù hé jiànzhù shǐyòng shuǐní, bōli děng cáiliào, zhèxiē cáiliào báitiān xīshōu rèliàng, yèjiān zài huǎnmàn de shìfàng chūlai.
lines.en: There are several causes. First, the city's many roads and buildings use materials like concrete and glass, which absorb heat by day and slowly release it at night.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 其次，高楼密集，阻碍了空气流通，热量难以扩散。
lines.py: Qícì, gāolóu mìjí, zǔ'ài le kōngqì liútōng, rèliàng nányǐ kuòsàn.
lines.en: Second, tall buildings are packed closely together, blocking air flow so the heat can't disperse.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 再次，空调、汽车和工厂排放的热量，也进一步推高了城市的温度。
lines.py: Zàicì, kōngtiáo, qìchē hé gōngchǎng páifàng de rèliàng, yě jìn yí bù tuīgāo le chéngshì de wēndù.
lines.en: Third, heat given off by air conditioners, cars and factories pushes city temperatures even higher.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 热岛效应带来的影响不容忽视。气温升高会增加能源消耗，夏天用电高峰时，电网的压力会明显加大。
lines.py: Rèdǎo xiàoyìng dàilai de yǐngxiǎng bùróng hūshì. Qìwēn shēnggāo huì zēngjiā néngyuán xiāohào, xiàtiān yòng diàn gāofēng shí, diànwǎng de yālì huì míngxiǎn jiādà.
lines.en: The effects can't be ignored. Higher temperatures raise energy use, and at summer peak times the strain on the power grid grows noticeably.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 此外，高温还会加剧空气污染，给老人和儿童的日常生活带来不便。
lines.py: Cǐwài, gāowēn hái huì jiājù kōngqì wūrǎn, gěi lǎorén hé értóng de rìcháng shēnghuó dàilai búbiàn.
lines.en: Heat also makes air pollution worse and makes daily life harder for older people and children.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 那么，城市应当如何应对呢？目前，许多城市采取的办法主要有三种。
lines.py: Nàme, chéngshì yīngdāng rúhé yìngduì ne? Mùqián, xǔduō chéngshì cǎiqǔ de bànfǎ zhǔyào yǒu sān zhǒng.
lines.en: So how should cities respond? At present, most cities take three main approaches.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 一是扩大绿地和水面的面积。研究表明，大型公园内部的温度往往比周围街区低两到三度。
lines.py: Yī shì kuòdà lǜdì hé shuǐmiàn de miànjī. Yánjiū biǎomíng, dàxíng gōngyuán nèibù de wēndù wǎngwǎng bǐ zhōuwéi jiēqū dī liǎng dào sān dù.
lines.en: One is to expand green space and water surfaces. Studies show the inside of a large park is often two to three degrees cooler than the streets around it.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 二是推广楼顶绿化和颜色较浅的材料，减少建筑对阳光的吸收。
lines.py: Èr shì tuīguǎng lóudǐng lǜhuà hé yánsè jiào qiǎn de cáiliào, jiǎnshǎo jiànzhù duì yángguāng de xīshōu.
lines.en: Two is to promote green roofs and light-coloured materials so buildings absorb less sunlight.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 三是在城市规划中留下“通风走廊”，让郊区的凉风能够进入城市中心。
lines.py: Sān shì zài chéngshì guīhuà zhōng liúxià “tōngfēng zǒuláng”, ràng jiāoqū de liángfēng nénggòu jìnrù chéngshì zhōngxīn.
lines.en: Three is to leave “ventilation corridors” in city planning so cool air from the suburbs can reach the centre.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 教授，您提到的这些措施，成本是不是很高？普通城市能负担得起吗？
lines.py: Jiàoshòu, nín tídào de zhèxiē cuòshī, chéngběn shì bu shì hěn gāo? Pǔtōng chéngshì néng fùdān de qǐ ma?
lines.en: Professor, aren't these measures very expensive? Can an ordinary city afford them?

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 这是一个很实际的问题。大规模改造确实需要大量投入，但像楼顶绿化、种植行道树这样的措施，可以分阶段进行，投入相对有限。
lines.py: Zhè shì yí ge hěn shíjì de wèntí. Dà guīmó gǎizào quèshí xūyào dàliàng tóurù, dàn xiàng lóudǐng lǜhuà, zhòngzhí xíngdàoshù zhèyàng de cuòshī, kěyǐ fēn jiēduàn jìnxíng, tóurù xiāngduì yǒuxiàn.
lines.en: A very practical question. Large-scale rebuilding does need heavy investment, but measures like green roofs and planting street trees can be done in stages at relatively modest cost.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 更重要的是，从长远来看，降低能源消耗所节省的费用，往往能够抵消前期的投入。
lines.py: Gèng zhòngyào de shì, cóng chángyuǎn lái kàn, jiàngdī néngyuán xiāohào suǒ jiéshěng de fèiyong, wǎngwǎng nénggòu dǐxiāo qiánqī de tóurù.
lines.en: More importantly, in the long run the money saved by using less energy often offsets the initial spending.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 下节课，我们将以几个具体城市作为例子，比较不同做法的效果。
lines.py: Xià jié kè, wǒmen jiāng yǐ jǐ ge jùtǐ chéngshì zuòwéi lìzi, bǐjiào bùtóng zuòfǎ de xiàoguǒ.
lines.en: Next class we'll take a few specific cities as examples and compare how well different approaches work.

title: Older consumers and the market
scene: A TV host interviews an economist about an ageing population

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 观众朋友们好。近年来，老年人消费市场成为一个热门话题。今天我们请到了一位经济学家，跟大家聊聊这个问题。
lines.py: Guānzhòng péngyoumen hǎo. Jìnnián lái, lǎoniánrén xiāofèi shìchǎng chéngwéi yí ge rèmén huàtí. Jīntiān wǒmen qǐngdào le yí wèi jīngjìxuéjiā, gēn dàjiā liáoliao zhège wèntí.
lines.en: Hello, viewers. In recent years the market for older consumers has become a hot topic. Today we have an economist here to talk about it.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 大家好，很高兴参加今天的节目。
lines.py: Dàjiā hǎo, hěn gāoxìng cānjiā jīntiān de jiémù.
lines.en: Hello, everyone. I'm glad to be on the programme.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 首先请您解释一下，为什么老年人消费市场越来越受到关注？
lines.py: Shǒuxiān qǐng nín jiěshì yíxià, wèi shénme lǎoniánrén xiāofèi shìchǎng yuè lái yuè shòudào guānzhù?
lines.en: First, could you explain why this market is getting more and more attention?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 最直接的原因是人口结构的变化。随着平均寿命延长、出生率下降，老年人在总人口中所占的比例不断上升。
lines.py: Zuì zhíjiē de yuányīn shì rénkǒu jiégòu de biànhuà. Suízhe píngjūn shòumìng yáncháng, chūshēnglǜ xiàjiàng, lǎoniánrén zài zǒng rénkǒu zhōng suǒ zhàn de bǐlì búduàn shàngshēng.
lines.en: The most direct reason is the change in population structure. As life expectancy rises and the birth rate falls, older people make up an ever larger share of the population.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 与此同时，如今的老年人和二三十年前相比，受教育程度更高，收入和储蓄也更有保障，消费能力明显增强。
lines.py: Yǔ cǐ tóngshí, rújīn de lǎoniánrén hé èr sānshí nián qián xiāngbǐ, shòu jiàoyù chéngdù gèng gāo, shōurù hé chǔxù yě gèng yǒu bǎozhàng, xiāofèi nénglì míngxiǎn zēngqiáng.
lines.en: At the same time, compared with twenty or thirty years ago, today's older people are better educated, have more secure income and savings, and clearly greater spending power.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 那他们的消费需求有哪些新特点？
lines.py: Nà tāmen de xiāofèi xūqiú yǒu nǎxiē xīn tèdiǎn?
lines.en: What's new about what they want to buy?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 过去人们普遍认为，老年人的消费主要集中在吃和穿上。但现在，旅游、学习、文化娱乐等方面的支出增长很快。
lines.py: Guòqù rénmen pǔbiàn rènwéi, lǎoniánrén de xiāofèi zhǔyào jízhōng zài chī hé chuān shang. Dàn xiànzài, lǚyóu, xuéxí, wénhuà yúlè děng fāngmiàn de zhīchū zēngzhǎng hěn kuài.
lines.en: People used to assume older people spent mainly on food and clothing. Now spending on travel, learning, culture and entertainment is growing fast.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 比如，不少城市的老年大学一位难求，书法、摄影、外语课程报名都要排队。
lines.py: Bǐrú, bù shǎo chéngshì de lǎonián dàxué yí wèi nán qiú, shūfǎ, shèyǐng, wàiyǔ kèchéng bàomíng dōu yào páiduì.
lines.en: In many cities, for example, places at universities for seniors are hard to get, and people queue to sign up for calligraphy, photography and language courses.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 那么企业在进入这个市场时，面临哪些挑战？
lines.py: Nàme qǐyè zài jìnrù zhège shìchǎng shí, miànlín nǎxiē tiǎozhàn?
lines.en: So what challenges do companies face when entering this market?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 最大的问题在于，很多企业对老年人的理解还停留在过去的印象上。产品设计要么过于复杂，要么把老年人当成弱者，忽视了他们追求品质和尊严的心理。
lines.py: Zuì dà de wèntí zàiyú, hěn duō qǐyè duì lǎoniánrén de lǐjiě hái tíngliú zài guòqù de yìnxiàng shang. Chǎnpǐn shèjì yàome guòyú fùzá, yàome bǎ lǎoniánrén dàngchéng ruòzhě, hūshì le tāmen zhuīqiú pǐnzhì hé zūnyán de xīnlǐ.
lines.en: The biggest problem is that many companies still see older people through outdated images. Products are either too complicated or treat older people as weak, ignoring their wish for quality and dignity.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 能举个例子吗？
lines.py: Néng jǔ ge lìzi ma?
lines.en: Could you give an example?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 比如有些手机为了方便老人，把字体放得很大，颜色也很鲜艳，但不少老人反而不愿意用，觉得这是在给自己贴标签。
lines.py: Bǐrú yǒuxiē shǒujī wèile fāngbiàn lǎorén, bǎ zìtǐ fàng de hěn dà, yánsè yě hěn xiānyàn, dàn bù shǎo lǎorén fǎn'ér bú yuànyì yòng, juéde zhè shì zài gěi zìjǐ tiē biāoqiān.
lines.en: Some phones, to be easy for older users, have huge fonts and bright colours, yet many older people refuse to use them because it feels like being labelled.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 您对企业有什么建议？
lines.py: Nín duì qǐyè yǒu shénme jiànyì?
lines.en: What would you advise companies to do?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 关键是要真正走近这个群体，在设计阶段就请老年用户参与进来，而不是凭想象去开发产品。
lines.py: Guānjiàn shì yào zhēnzhèng zǒujìn zhège qúntǐ, zài shèjì jiēduàn jiù qǐng lǎonián yònghù cānyù jìnlai, ér bú shì píng xiǎngxiàng qù kāifā chǎnpǐn.
lines.en: The key is to really get close to this group and bring older users in at the design stage, instead of developing products from imagination.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 最后，您怎么看这个市场的前景？
lines.py: Zuìhòu, nín zěnme kàn zhège shìchǎng de qiánjǐng?
lines.en: Finally, how do you see the outlook for this market?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 我认为潜力巨大，但它不是一个可以快速赚钱的市场。只有长期投入、真正赢得信任的企业，才能获得持续的发展。
lines.py: Wǒ rènwéi qiánlì jùdà, dàn tā bú shì yí ge kěyǐ kuàisù zhuàn qián de shìchǎng. Zhǐyǒu chángqī tóurù, zhēnzhèng yíngdé xìnrèn de qǐyè, cái néng huòdé chíxù de fāzhǎn.
lines.en: I think the potential is huge, but it isn't a market for quick money. Only companies that invest for the long term and truly earn trust will keep growing.

title: Keeping a weaving craft alive
scene: A radio feature with a researcher and a scholar on recording traditional crafts

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 在西南某省的一个山村里，一位七十多岁的老人每天仍坚持在织布的机器前工作。她织的布图案复杂、色彩丰富，这种技艺已经在当地流传了几百年。
lines.py: Zài xīnán mǒu shěng de yí ge shāncūn li, yí wèi qīshí duō suì de lǎorén měi tiān réng jiānchí zài zhī bù de jīqì qián gōngzuò. Tā zhī de bù tú'àn fùzá, sècǎi fēngfù, zhè zhǒng jìyì yǐjīng zài dāngdì liúchuán le jǐ bǎi nián.
lines.en: In a mountain village in a south-western province, a woman in her seventies still works at her loom every day. Her cloth has intricate patterns and rich colours, a skill passed down locally for centuries.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 然而，随着年轻人纷纷外出打工，愿意学习这门手艺的人越来越少。老人担心，这门技艺可能会在她这一代失传。
lines.py: Rán'ér, suízhe niánqīngrén fēnfēn wàichū dǎgōng, yuànyì xuéxí zhè mén shǒuyì de rén yuè lái yuè shǎo. Lǎorén dānxīn, zhè mén jìyì kěnéng huì zài tā zhè yí dài shīchuán.
lines.en: But as young people leave one after another to work elsewhere, fewer and fewer want to learn the craft. She fears it may be lost with her generation.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 这样的情况并非个别现象。据统计，在已经列入保护名录的传统技艺中，相当一部分传承人的年龄超过六十岁。
lines.py: Zhèyàng de qíngkuàng bìngfēi gèbié xiànxiàng. Jù tǒngjì, zài yǐjīng lièrù bǎohù mínglù de chuántǒng jìyì zhōng, xiāngdāng yí bùfen chuánchéngrén de niánlíng chāoguò liùshí suì.
lines.en: This is not an isolated case. Figures show that among traditional crafts already on the protection list, a large share of the master practitioners are over sixty.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 面对这一困境，一些研究机构开始尝试用数字技术为传统技艺建立档案。
lines.py: Miànduì zhè yí kùnjìng, yìxiē yánjiū jīgòu kāishǐ chángshì yòng shùzì jìshù wèi chuántǒng jìyì jiànlì dàng'àn.
lines.en: Faced with this, some research institutes have begun using digital technology to build archives of traditional crafts.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 我们的工作主要分为三步。第一步是高清拍摄，把每一道工序都完整地记录下来。
lines.py: Wǒmen de gōngzuò zhǔyào fēnwéi sān bù. Dì yī bù shì gāoqīng pāishè, bǎ měi yí dào gōngxù dōu wánzhěng de jìlù xiàlai.
lines.en: Our work has three main steps. The first is high-definition filming that records every stage of the process in full.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 第二步是采访传承人，了解每个图案背后的故事和含义。很多知识从来没有写在纸上，只存在于老人的记忆里。
lines.py: Dì èr bù shì cǎifǎng chuánchéngrén, liǎojiě měi ge tú'àn bèihòu de gùshi hé hányì. Hěn duō zhīshi cónglái méiyǒu xiě zài zhǐ shang, zhǐ cúnzài yú lǎorén de jìyì li.
lines.en: The second is interviewing the practitioners to learn the stories and meanings behind each pattern. Much of this knowledge was never written down and exists only in their memories.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 第三步是把这些资料整理成数据库，向公众和研究者开放。
lines.py: Dì sān bù shì bǎ zhèxiē zīliào zhěnglǐ chéng shùjùkù, xiàng gōngzhòng hé yánjiūzhě kāifàng.
lines.en: The third is organising the material into a database open to the public and to researchers.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 不过，也有学者对此提出了不同的看法。
lines.py: Búguò, yě yǒu xuézhě duìcǐ tíchū le bùtóng de kànfǎ.
lines.en: Some scholars, however, see it differently.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 数字记录当然很有价值，但我们必须清醒地认识到，录像保存的只是技艺的外形。
lines.py: Shùzì jìlù dāngrán hěn yǒu jiàzhí, dàn wǒmen bìxū qīngxǐng de rènshi dào, lùxiàng bǎocún de zhǐ shì jìyì de wàixíng.
lines.en: Digital records are of course valuable, but we must be clear that video only preserves the outward form of a craft.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 手艺真正的灵魂在于人的手感和经验，这些东西只能在长期的实践中，通过师傅带徒弟的方式一代代传下去。
lines.py: Shǒuyì zhēnzhèng de línghún zàiyú rén de shǒugǎn hé jīngyàn, zhèxiē dōngxi zhǐ néng zài chángqī de shíjiàn zhōng, tōngguò shīfu dài túdì de fāngshì yí dài dài chuán xiàqu.
lines.en: The real soul of a craft lies in a person's feel and experience, which can only be handed down over years of practice, from master to apprentice, generation after generation.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 如果只有档案，没有人继续做，那这门技艺实际上就已经失去了生命。
lines.py: Rúguǒ zhǐ yǒu dàng'àn, méiyǒu rén jìxù zuò, nà zhè mén jìyì shíjì shang jiù yǐjīng shīqù le shēngmìng.
lines.en: If there is only an archive and nobody keeps practising, the craft has in effect already lost its life.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 对此，研究人员也表示认同。他们正在与当地学校合作开设兴趣课程，并帮助手艺人通过网络销售作品，让这门技艺能够带来实际收入。
lines.py: Duìcǐ, yánjiū rényuán yě biǎoshì rèntóng. Tāmen zhèngzài yǔ dāngdì xuéxiào hézuò kāishè xìngqù kèchéng, bìng bāngzhù shǒuyìrén tōngguò wǎngluò xiāoshòu zuòpǐn, ràng zhè mén jìyì nénggòu dàilai shíjì shōurù.
lines.en: The researchers agree. They are working with local schools to run interest classes and helping craftspeople sell their work online, so the craft can bring in real income.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 我们希望年轻人看到，传统手艺不只是过去的东西，也可以是一种有前途的职业。
lines.py: Wǒmen xīwàng niánqīngrén kàndào, chuántǒng shǒuyì bù zhǐ shì guòqù de dōngxi, yě kěyǐ shì yì zhǒng yǒu qiántú de zhíyè.
lines.en: We want young people to see that a traditional craft isn't just a thing of the past. It can also be a career with a future.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 保护与发展如何结合，或许是每一项传统技艺都要面对的问题。
lines.py: Bǎohù yǔ fāzhǎn rúhé jiéhé, huòxǔ shì měi yí xiàng chuántǒng jìyì dōu yào miànduì de wèntí.
lines.en: How to combine protection with development may be a question every traditional craft has to face.

title: Cutting food waste
scene: A radio programme with a researcher and a restaurant industry representative

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 欢迎收听本期节目。据有关机构估算，全球每年生产的食物中，约有三分之一在生产、运输和消费过程中被损失或浪费。今天我们请到两位嘉宾，一起探讨如何减少食物浪费。
lines.py: Huānyíng shōutīng běn qī jiémù. Jù yǒuguān jīgòu gūsuàn, quánqiú měi nián shēngchǎn de shíwù zhōng, yuē yǒu sān fēn zhī yī zài shēngchǎn, yùnshū hé xiāofèi guòchéng zhōng bèi sǔnshī huò làngfèi. Jīntiān wǒmen qǐngdào liǎng wèi jiābīn, yìqǐ tàntǎo rúhé jiǎnshǎo shíwù làngfèi.
lines.en: Welcome to this week's programme. Estimates suggest that about a third of the food produced worldwide each year is lost or wasted during production, transport and consumption. Today two guests join us to discuss how to cut food waste.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 很多人以为食物浪费主要发生在吃饭的时候，其实并不完全是这样。在发展中国家，相当一部分损失发生在储存和运输环节，比如缺少冷藏设施，蔬菜水果在路上就坏了。
lines.py: Hěn duō rén yǐwéi shíwù làngfèi zhǔyào fāshēng zài chīfàn de shíhou, qíshí bìng bù wánquán shì zhèyàng. Zài fāzhǎnzhōng guójiā, xiāngdāng yí bùfen sǔnshī fāshēng zài chǔcún hé yùnshū huánjié, bǐrú quēshǎo lěngcáng shèshī, shūcài shuǐguǒ zài lù shang jiù huài le.
lines.en: Many people think food waste happens mainly when we eat, but that's not the whole story. In developing countries a large share of losses happen in storage and transport. Without cold storage, for example, vegetables and fruit spoil on the way.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 而在发达国家，浪费更多集中在零售和消费环节。超市为了让货架看起来整齐美观，会把外形不完美的产品淘汰掉；家庭则常常买得太多，最后吃不完扔掉。
lines.py: Ér zài fādá guójiā, làngfèi gèng duō jízhōng zài língshòu hé xiāofèi huánjié. Chāoshì wèile ràng huòjià kàn qilai zhěngqí měiguān, huì bǎ wàixíng bù wánměi de chǎnpǐn táotài diào; jiātíng zé chángcháng mǎi de tài duō, zuìhòu chī bu wán rēngdiào.
lines.en: In developed countries, waste is concentrated more in retail and consumption. Supermarkets reject imperfect-looking produce to keep shelves neat, and households often buy too much and throw away what they can't finish.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 那么在餐饮行业，情况又如何呢？
lines.py: Nàme zài cānyǐn hángyè, qíngkuàng yòu rúhé ne?
lines.en: And what about the restaurant industry?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 餐饮行业的浪费确实比较突出。一方面，有些顾客点菜时讲面子，宁可多点也不愿意少点；另一方面，不少餐厅为了显得大方，菜的分量做得过大。
lines.py: Cānyǐn hángyè de làngfèi quèshí bǐjiào tūchū. Yì fāngmiàn, yǒuxiē gùkè diǎn cài shí jiǎng miànzi, nìngkě duō diǎn yě bú yuànyì shǎo diǎn; lìng yì fāngmiàn, bù shǎo cāntīng wèile xiǎnde dàfang, cài de fènliàng zuò de guò dà.
lines.en: Waste in restaurants is indeed a real problem. On one hand, some diners order to save face and would rather order too much than too little. On the other, many restaurants make portions too large to look generous.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 近几年，我们行业推出了一些做法，比如提供小份菜、半份菜，主动提醒顾客适量点菜，还鼓励打包。
lines.py: Jìn jǐ nián, wǒmen hángyè tuīchū le yìxiē zuòfǎ, bǐrú tígōng xiǎo fèn cài, bàn fèn cài, zhǔdòng tíxǐng gùkè shìliàng diǎn cài, hái gǔlì dǎbāo.
lines.en: In recent years our industry has introduced some practices, such as small and half portions, reminding diners to order sensibly, and encouraging them to take leftovers home.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 这些措施效果怎么样？
lines.py: Zhèxiē cuòshī xiàoguǒ zěnmeyàng?
lines.en: How well have these measures worked?

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 总体来说，效果是积极的。我们协会调查的餐厅中，推出小份菜以后，剩菜量平均减少了大约两成。
lines.py: Zǒngtǐ lái shuō, xiàoguǒ shì jījí de. Wǒmen xiéhuì diàochá de cāntīng zhōng, tuīchū xiǎo fèn cài yǐhòu, shèngcài liàng píngjūn jiǎnshǎo le dàyuē liǎng chéng.
lines.en: Overall, the results are positive. Among the restaurants our association surveyed, leftovers fell by about twenty percent on average after small portions were introduced.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 但也有餐厅反映，小份菜的成本并没有按比例下降，利润反而变薄了，所以推广起来有一定阻力。
lines.py: Dàn yě yǒu cāntīng fǎnyìng, xiǎo fèn cài de chéngběn bìng méiyǒu àn bǐlì xiàjiàng, lìrùn fǎn'ér biàn báo le, suǒyǐ tuīguǎng qilai yǒu yídìng zǔlì.
lines.en: But some restaurants report that the cost of a small portion doesn't drop in proportion, so margins get thinner, and that creates some resistance.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 我觉得这恰恰说明，减少浪费不能只靠企业自觉，还需要制度上的支持，比如对积极参与的企业给予一定的政策优惠。
lines.py: Wǒ juéde zhè qiàqià shuōmíng, jiǎnshǎo làngfèi bù néng zhǐ kào qǐyè zìjué, hái xūyào zhìdù shang de zhīchí, bǐrú duì jījí cānyù de qǐyè jǐyǔ yídìng de zhèngcè yōuhuì.
lines.en: I think that shows exactly why cutting waste can't rely on businesses' goodwill alone. It needs institutional support too, such as policy incentives for companies that take part.

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 另外，临期食品的问题也值得重视。很多食品离保质期还有一段时间，质量完全没有问题，但因为不好卖就被处理掉了。
lines.py: Lìngwài, línqī shípǐn de wèntí yě zhídé zhòngshì. Hěn duō shípǐn lí bǎozhìqī hái yǒu yí duàn shíjiān, zhìliàng wánquán méiyǒu wèntí, dàn yīnwèi bù hǎo mài jiù bèi chǔlǐ diào le.
lines.en: Food near its best-before date also deserves attention. Much of it still has time left and is perfectly fine, but it gets thrown out because it's hard to sell.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 这一点我同意。现在已经出现了一些专门销售临期食品的商店，价格便宜，很受年轻人欢迎。这既减少了浪费，又让消费者得到了实惠。
lines.py: Zhè yì diǎn wǒ tóngyì. Xiànzài yǐjīng chūxiàn le yìxiē zhuānmén xiāoshòu línqī shípǐn de shāngdiàn, jiàgé piányi, hěn shòu niánqīngrén huānyíng. Zhè jì jiǎnshǎo le làngfèi, yòu ràng xiāofèizhě dédào le shíhuì.
lines.en: I agree on that. There are now shops that specialise in near-date food. They're cheap and popular with young people, which cuts waste and gives shoppers a real saving.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 最后，请两位嘉宾分别给听众提一个简单的建议。
lines.py: Zuìhòu, qǐng liǎng wèi jiābīn fēnbié gěi tīngzhòng tí yí ge jiǎndān de jiànyì.
lines.en: Finally, could each of you give listeners one simple piece of advice?

lines.speaker: 女
lines.zh: 买东西之前先看看冰箱，按需购买。
lines.py: Mǎi dōngxi zhīqián xiān kànkan bīngxiāng, àn xū gòumǎi.
lines.en: Check your fridge before you shop, and buy only what you need.

lines.speaker: 男
lines.zh: 在外面吃饭，吃多少点多少，吃不完就打包。
lines.py: Zài wàimiàn chīfàn, chī duōshao diǎn duōshao, chī bu wán jiù dǎbāo.
lines.en: When eating out, order what you'll eat, and take home what you can't finish.

lines.speaker: 旁白
lines.zh: 感谢两位嘉宾。减少浪费，从每个人的一顿饭开始。
lines.py: Gǎnxiè liǎng wèi jiābīn. Jiǎnshǎo làngfèi, cóng měi ge rén de yí dùn fàn kāishǐ.
lines.en: Thank you both. Cutting waste starts with each person's next meal.
